raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Remove `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` and always select the DCP multi-token (spec-decode) verify kernel heuristically.

Default behavior is unchanged: the builder now always does what `auto` (the default) did.

- **gfx950:** AITER round-robin asm decode (cprr) when the DCP-gathered head count pads to a native kernel (16/32/64/128), otherwise segmented MLA.
- **gfx942:** segmented MLA where it fits in LDS, otherwise Triton split-KV decode. The env var never affected gfx942.

What goes away:
- `segmented`: the opt-out from cprr on gfx950.
- `asm`: the hard error for head counts cprr can't serve. These now fall back to segmented, as `auto` already did. A config with neither kernel still fails at builder init.

This also clears the way for a follow-up gfx942 verify-kernel work to choose a new assembly verify kernel. 

## Test Plan

    pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_verify_gfx942.py \
           tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py

## Test Result

- Routing tests pass. Env-parsing and forced-override tests are removed; native head counts, K3's 96→128 padding, fallback above 128 heads, and off-gfx950 routing are covered.

## Accuracy validation on gfx942

Kimi-K3 + DSpark at TP8/DCP8 scores the same on GSM8K with and without this PR.

| Build | flexible-extract | strict-match | Mean acceptance length |
|---|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 4.19 |
| With this PR | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 0.9682 ± 0.0048 | 4.19 |

### Setup

- 8x AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942)
- Model: `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (MXFP4) with the `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` draft
- Attention backends: `ROCM_AITER_MLA` for the target, `TRITON_MLA` for the draft
- The two runs differ only by this PR. Server flags, eval command and environment are identical.

### Server

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
  --served-model-name kimi-k3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --max-model-len 65536 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
  --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention_backend": "TRITON_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}' \
  --port 8000
```

### Eval (lm_eval 0.4.13)

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args '{"model": "kimi-k3", "base_url": "http://localhost:8000/v1/completions", "num_concurrent": 32, "max_retries": 10, "max_gen_toks": 2048, "tokenizer_backend": "None", "tokenized_requests": "False"}' \
  --tasks gsm8k --batch_size auto --num_fewshot 20 --trust_remote_code
```

### Notes

- **Why no change is expected:** `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` never affected gfx942. On gfx942 the verify route is chosen the same way before and after this PR.

## Accuracy validation on gfx950

| Build | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Without this PR | 0.9598 | 0.9591 |
| With this PR | 0.9575 | 0.9583 |

### Server

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --served_model_name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
    --kv_cache_dtype fp8 \
    --tensor_parallel_size 8 \
    --trust_remote_code \
    --mm_encoder_tp_mode data \
    --mm_encoder_attn_backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 8000 \
    --max_model_len 131072 \
    --max_num_batched_tokens 16384 \
    --max_num_seqs 256 \
    --max_cudagraph_capture_size 512 \
    --no_enable_prefix_caching \
    --no-enable_log_requests \
    --enable_auto_tool_choice \
    --async_scheduling \
    --compilation_config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
    --tool_call_parser kimi_k3 \
    --decode_context_parallel_size 8 \
    --dcp_comm_backend a2a \
    --speculative_config '{"method": "dspark", "model": "Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark", "num_speculative_tokens": 5, "attention_backend": "ROCM_AITER_MLA", "draft_sample_method": "probabilistic", "rejection_sample_method": "block"}'
```

nodes.body: Thanks for the review @simondanielsson ! I'll post some accuracy numbers tomorrow.
Hi @simondanielsson ! Thanks again for the feedback. I have updated now the description with accuracy numbers both for gfx950 and gfx942.

@simondanielsson Yes. On gfx950 there is no shape where cprr can run and segmented is faster, so the variable is not an escape hatch for a slow cprr.

Segmented remains only where cprr has no kernel: query length below 3, gathered heads that do not pad to 16/32/64/128, or off gfx950. auto already used that fallback. Setting segmented only redirected batches cprr can serve, and that route is slower because it expands every verify token into its own paged-KV row.

I haven't benched myself on gfx950, but on Kimi-K3, 8× MI355X, TP8/DCP8 (96 heads padded to 128), from the PRs that enabled cprr:

[#56861](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56861), ISL 100k / OSL 256, qlen 8: mean TPOT 22.1 ms to 10.9 ms at concurrency 1, 53.1 ms to 15.6 ms at concurrency 4, and 179 ms to 110 ms at concurrency 8. At qlen 2 the two settings match within noise, because both run segmented.
[#59965](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59965), concurrency 48: segmented 141.0 tok/s and 170.8 ms median TPOT, cprr 212.6 tok/s and 101.0 ms. At OSL 1024 segmented finished no request inside the window.

GSM8K stayed within one standard error. Removing the override only drops the slower opt-out.

issue_comments.body: Thanks for the review @simondanielsson ! I'll post some accuracy numbers tomorrow.
Hi @simondanielsson ! Thanks again for the feedback. I have updated now the description with accuracy numbers both for gfx950 and gfx942.

@simondanielsson Yes. On gfx950 there is no shape where cprr can run and segmented is faster, so the variable is not an escape hatch for a slow cprr.

Segmented remains only where cprr has no kernel: query length below 3, gathered heads that do not pad to 16/32/64/128, or off gfx950. auto already used that fallback. Setting segmented only redirected batches cprr can serve, and that route is slower because it expands every verify token into its own paged-KV row.

I haven't benched myself on gfx950, but on Kimi-K3, 8× MI355X, TP8/DCP8 (96 heads padded to 128), from the PRs that enabled cprr:

[#56861](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56861), ISL 100k / OSL 256, qlen 8: mean TPOT 22.1 ms to 10.9 ms at concurrency 1, 53.1 ms to 15.6 ms at concurrency 4, and 179 ms to 110 ms at concurrency 8. At qlen 2 the two settings match within noise, because both run segmented.
[#59965](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59965), concurrency 48: segmented 141.0 tok/s and 170.8 ms median TPOT, cprr 212.6 tok/s and 101.0 ms. At OSL 1024 segmented finished no request inside the window.

GSM8K stayed within one standard error. Removing the override only drops the slower opt-out.
